newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on profit-taking.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early firmness and closed softer for the first time in nine sessions at the close on Thursday after dealers took profits and bought dollars in advance of closing their books for the first half, traders said.
"They took profits after the strong advance in recent days," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 4 and 3.6 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9430/7.9460 and 7.9330/7.9360 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed trade mid-morning 0.6 of a centavo firmer at 7.8970/7.9020 per dollar.
Some dealers said the peso also weakened because several brokers who had gone short on dollars in recent days decided to take advantage of a relatively cheap dollar to square their books.
"It was a normal turnaround. Demand was not very heavy, it's just that volume is a little thin," another trader said.
"This morning everyone waited to see when others began to buy dollars before doing the same," he added.
Traders situated support for the peso after Thursday's session at 7.9530 per dollar.
